solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Outlaw pleased he's abandoned country

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
pleased means glad

indicators.note: abandoned in the sense of wild or uninhibited, so the letters of he's are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A happy man drops a prohibited plan and leaves a nation behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangladesh is a nation in South Asia, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Commander these days on the French border to the north

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the north means these letters are read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: la is French for the
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A naval chief now patrols the frontier with France to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns LARIM into MIRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a senior naval officer who commands a fleet.

clue.text: Worried trapped in empty ground with barrier

indicators.note: trapped in says the first piece is enclosed by the second
an empty word keeps only its outside letters, so ground loses everything between its ends

parts.note: something that worried you ate at you

explanation.surface: Someone anxious is stuck on a patch of bare land behind a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A gated road or community has a gate across it, a barrier controlling entry.

clue.text: Pass, disregarding top ten in Le Monde supplement

indicators.note: ignoring the top of a down entry means dropping its first letter

parts.note: to come to pass is to happen
dix is French for ten, Le Monde being a French newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's extra section skips its top ten list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarding top' takes the H from HAPPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is extra matter added at the end of a book, a supplement to the main text.

clue.text: Modelled this range around milliner that's critical

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters go round the hat-maker
modelled means shaped or moulded, so the letters of this range are reshaped

parts.note: a milliner makes hats, so is a hatter

explanation.surface: A collection of hats is shown off around a hat-maker at a fashion show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modelled' makes EARTHSING from THIS RANGE; 'milliner' looks like the person modelling, but supplies the inserted letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earth-shattering is momentous, of crucial importance, as critical events are.

clue.text: One acting poorly over rent settlement

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting performer
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A bad actor is behind with the rent for his lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places the first piece above the second in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small village, a tiny settlement.

clue.text: Person depressed device for cleaner energy

parts.note: a mop is a cleaner's tool
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A gloomy person wants a cleaning gadget that saves power.
explanation.definitionFit: A mope is someone who broods listlessly, a gloomy, dejected sort.

clue.text: One with stomach upset delayed, day ruined

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so these letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
tum is an informal word for stomach
delayed means late

explanation.surface: Someone with an upset stomach was held up and their day was spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutilated means badly damaged or disfigured, so ruined.

clue.text: A regular forgetting second uniform inspection

parts.note: a as in 'five pounds a day' means per

indicators.note: forgetting the second one means the later of the two U letters is left out

parts.note: regular means usual
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A routine uniform inspection skips a second look.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination of something.

clue.text: Leak unfortunate pitmen uncovered

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled
uncovered means the covering outer letters of pitmen are stripped off

explanation.surface: A gas leak exposes unlucky miners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' leaves ITME from PITMEN; 'unfortunate' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or discharge, as a leak lets something out.

clue.text: Gunners and me restricted by posh old man's guidelines

indicators.note: restricted by says these pieces are hemmed in by the father

parts.note: pater is a posh, old-fashioned word for father
RA, the Royal Artillery, are the gunners
the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Soldiers and I are kept in line by a toffee-nosed father's rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Parameters are the limits or boundaries within which something operates, its guiding rules.

clue.text: Writer's uninteresting study

parts.note: dry means dull or uninteresting
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: An author's study is a dull place.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is'. John Dryden was a 17th-century English poet and dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a major English poet and playwright, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Rash is undesired with head becoming hot

indicators.note: with its head becoming says the first letter is swapped for a new one

parts.note: something undesired is not needed, needless
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An unwanted skin rash flares up and turns your head hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint; it is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means careless and thoughtless, acting without regard to consequences, as a rash person does.

clue.text: Portly clod is occupying pub

indicators.note: occupying says these pieces sit inside the pub

parts.note: PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub
a clod is a lump of earth

explanation.surface: A stout oaf is propping up the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumpish means somewhat fat, a little stout, which is what portly means.

clue.text: Checked daughter after Mint Oreo goes astray

indicators.note: after puts the daughter at the end
something that goes astray wanders off course, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A parent keeps an eye on a daughter after a cookie goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To have monitored something is to have watched or kept a check on it.

clue.text: Listened to back story

indicators.note: listened to says the word for back is heard rather than spelt, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the tail is the back end of something

explanation.surface: Hearing about the backstory of a character.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a narrative, an account of events, real or imagined.

clue.text: Cover vegetable boxes strewn around shed

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the vegetable surrounds the other letters

parts.note: beet is a root vegetable

indicators.note: strewn around means scattered about, so the letters of shed are mixed up

explanation.surface: Crates of vegetables lie scattered around the garden shed under a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsheet is a cloth spread over a bed, a bed covering.

clue.text: One shot in EastEnders

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the name of the soap

explanation.surface: Someone gets shot in an episode of the TV soap.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap opera set in London. The Sten was a British submachine gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sten is a gun, something that fires, so a thing that shoots, one shot.

clue.text: As a result, article on eBay oddly disappeared

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means on, concerning

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of eBay vanish, so only the even ones are kept

explanation.surface: An item listed online vanished strangely, with consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby means by that means, in consequence of that.

clue.text: Pressing foot traffic covering England's capital

indicators.note: covering says the trade word wraps round the letter

parts.note: to traffic is to trade, so traffic as a noun is trading

indicators.note: the capital or head letter of England's is its first

explanation.surface: Pushing the pedal hard in the traffic of England's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading is pressing down with the foot, as when treading grapes.

clue.text: Recent information across page on that man's relatives

indicators.note: across means stretching over, so the news goes round the other pieces

parts.note: news is recent information
he refers to that man

explanation.surface: The latest gossip about a page on a man's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephews are a sibling's sons, so they are family members, kin.

clue.text: Package trucker regularly brought into China

indicators.note: brought into says the picked letters are placed inside the mate

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of trucker

explanation.surface: A lorry driver routinely delivers a package to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; Cockney rhyming slang china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a wrapped package sent by post or courier.

clue.text: Heard event outside of Santa Fe food repository

indicators.note: heard says the word for the event is spoken, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: a meet is a sporting event, such as an athletics meeting

indicators.note: outside of picks the outer letters of Santa

explanation.surface: A rumoured event takes place on the outskirts of Santa Fe near a food store.
explanation.walkthrough: A meat safe is a ventilated cupboard for storing food before refrigerators were common.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat safe is a cupboard with mesh sides for keeping food, a store for provisions.

clue.text: Having developed following, street band

indicators.note: following puts the matured word after the street abbreviation

parts.note: ripe means fully developed or matured

explanation.surface: A street band that has developed a following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a group of musicians; here it is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow strip of colour, a band.

clue.text: Concrete over top of marshy land

parts.note: concrete means real, actual

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of marshy in this down clue

explanation.surface: Concrete poured on boggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, a land ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Cite advert broadcast as disparaging

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread and reordered

explanation.surface: Quote an advertisement put out on air as being belittling.
explanation.definitionFit: Detractive means tending to belittle or detract from someone's reputation, so disparaging.

clue.text: Experts taking away first in competitions

indicators.note: taking away the first letter means dropping the start of the word for contests

parts.note: races are competitions

explanation.surface: Specialists win prizes in contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are people highly skilled at something, top performers.

clue.text: Retreated once the journalist is observed

indicators.note: retreated means went backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe'
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: The reporter who once backed off is now being watched.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyed means looked at or watched, so observed.

clue.text: Sanction on Italy is interrupting season

parts.note: on is another name for the leg side in cricket
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: interrupting says is breaks into the word for season

parts.note: a season is a time, as in 'the time of year'

explanation.surface: An official approval for Italy breaks into the holiday season.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: To legitimise is to make lawful or authorise, which is to sanction.
